@graph.description: The night side of a song recorded twice: 2raumwohnung's 2017 single sets Inga Humpe's German verses and English refrain over a darker, 1980s-flavoured synth arrangement, one of two versions on their double album Nacht und Tag.
@graph.headline: 2raumwohnung - Somebody Lonely and Me (Nacht)

citation.name: ACRAZE cashes in on Cherish-sampled ID of the summer, 'Do It To It'

@graph.description: Orlando producer ACRAZE turned the vocal of Cherish's 2006 R&B single into a two-and-a-half-minute tech house track that spread through DJ sets before it was released and reached the UK top ten in 2022.
@graph.headline: ACRAZE - Do It To It (feat. Cherish)

@graph.description: Melodic synths crash into live drums and a snarling rock vocal: Do You opens Freeland's Cope with a breakbeat-punk jolt that sounds like a band and a DJ at war.
@graph.headline: Adam Freeland - Do You

inAlbum.name: Going Down In A Blaze Of Glory EP

@graph.name: Going Down In A Blaze Of Glory

citation.name: [DigitalDiamonds025] Alic - Going Down In A Blaze Of Glory EP
Going Down In A Blaze Of Glory (recording)

@graph.description: A seven-minute slab of psychedelic techno from the German duo Alic, released free on their own netlabel Digital Diamonds in 2012: punching drums under slowly shifting atmospheric layers.
@graph.headline: Alic - Going Down In A Blaze Of Glory

@graph.description: A twenty-year-old Alicia Keys at the piano, pouring gospel-sized yearning into a stark, minor-key confession about a love she cannot stop falling into.
@graph.headline: Alicia Keys - Fallin'

@graph.description: 'Forgotten Places' is a hushed downtempo piece by the Marseille producer Alif Tree, built around a sampled voice of the jazz singer Shirley Horn and released on Compost Records in 2006: nu-jazz that sounds like a memory being replayed.
@graph.headline: Alif Tree - Forgotten Places

citation.name: Alle Farben feat. Graham Candy – Sometimes (recording)

@graph.description: Alle Farben's sun-warmed deep house meets Graham Candy's quivering, unmistakable high voice in a wistful Berlin summer song about the days that do not go to plan.
@graph.headline: Alle Farben, Graham Candy - Sometimes

citation.name: Aloe Blacc Talks How to Make It in America Theme
Highsnobiety TV: An Evening with Aloe Blacc at MADE

@graph.description: A hard-times plea set to a Brooklyn retro-soul jam: Aloe Blacc's 2010 hit, the theme of HBO's How to Make It in America, heard here live in Berlin in 2011, where a chorus about a job lost and a dollar borrowed is made for a room to sing.
@graph.headline: Aloe Blacc - I Need a Dollar (Live)

@graph.description: A lullaby with teeth: alt-J's 2012 breakthrough wraps an obsessive love song, borrowed in part from Where the Wild Things Are, in plucked guitar, close harmonies and a refrain that piles up until it will not let go.
@graph.headline: Breezeblocks | alt-J (∆)

@graph.description: 'DJ' by Amanda Blank is a heartbreak song dressed as a club track: over a Diplo and Switch beat, the Philadelphia rapper asks the DJ to turn it up so she can dance a bad relationship away.
@graph.headline: Amanda Blank - DJ

@graph.description: A slinking, horn-stabbed confession of infidelity from Back to Black, written by Amy Winehouse and produced by Mark Ronson with the Dap-Kings' players: retro soul with a lyric no 1960s girl group would have sung.
@graph.headline: Amy Winehouse - You Know I'm No Good

@graph.description: Soft guitars, sibling harmonies and a daydream of flying away with someone: Big Jet Plane drifts in slowly and stays with you long after it lands.
@graph.headline: Angus & Julia Stone - Big Jet Plane

citation.name: Watch The Video For Anna Lunoe's Massive "Radioactive"
Anna Lunoe drops 'Radioactive' with new music video

@graph.description: Anna Lunoe's Radioactive, her 2016 debut on OWSLA, is a strobe-lit 'hyperhouse' banger sung in her own voice, all clipped vocal hooks, rave stabs and a low end built to rattle a festival tent.
@graph.headline: Anna Lunoe - Radioactive

@graph.name: Can't Get You Out of My Head (Cover)

citation.name: Can't Get You out of My Head (Cover) - AnnenMayKantereit x Parcels
Can't Get You Out of My Head

@graph.description: AnnenMayKantereit and Parcels join forces on a stripped-back cover of Kylie Minogue's 'Can't Get You Out of My Head', trading the original's cool electronic pulse for Henning May's rough voice and close band harmonies.
@graph.headline: Can't Get You Out of My Head (Cover) - AnnenMayKantereit x Parcels

@graph.description: A pulsating electro track from Anthony Rother's 2006 album Super Space Model on his own Datapunk label: machine rhythms, hard synthesizers and a chanted list of names that turns into the hook.
@graph.headline: Anthony Rother - Brainshaker

citation.name: The 20 best guitar riffs of the decade

@graph.description: A heavy, crawling riff, stomping handclaps and a late-night text that should never have been sent: Do I Wanna Know? turns romantic doubt into slow-burning swagger.
@graph.headline: Arctic Monkeys - Do I Wanna Know?

@graph.description: Arctic Monkeys turn a jealous late-night text into a riff-heavy stomp, with Alex Turner's rapid-fire wordplay riding a fuzzed-out, swaggering guitar line.
@graph.headline: Arctic Monkeys - R U Mine?

@graph.description: Alex Turner pleads with a lover to wake up from someone else's spell over a swaggering, hand-clapped shuffle and a chorus hook that sticks for days: the sixth single from AM.
@graph.headline: Arctic Monkeys - Snap Out Of It

citation.name: Asaf Avidan & The Mojos - The Reckoning

@graph.description: A cracked, ageless voice over a few acoustic chords: the original Reckoning Song from 2008 is a campfire confession about growing old, four years before Wankelmut's remix turned it into a European number one.
@graph.headline: Asaf Avidan & the Mojos - Reckoning Song (One Day)

@graph.description: The synth-heavy opener of Asian Dub Foundation's Tank: churning drum and bass, a dub-friendly chorus and the band's political urgency, at the start of an album written in the shadow of the Iraq War.
@graph.headline: Asian Dub Foundation - Flyover

citation.name: Volvo Cars' New Beginning brand campaign featuring Avicii goes live

@graph.description: Avicii wraps the standard Nina Simone made famous in soft, swelling synths and lets Audra Mae's smoky, soaring voice carry a song about new dawns, recorded for a 2015 film about his own recovery from years of touring.
@graph.headline: Avicii - Feeling Good

@graph.description: A slow, menacing electro-rock crawl that erupts into a howled confession, AWOLNATION's Sail is equal parts dread and release.
@graph.headline: AWOLNATION - Sail

citation.name: Feel the Vibe ('Til the Morning Comes)

@graph.description: Axwell's 2004 club record in its original long form: a pumping, filtered house groove that keeps building until the whole floor is lifted with it.
@graph.headline: Axwell - Feel The Vibe

citation.name: Axwell feat. Max'C – I Found U (radio edit)
Axwell feat. Max'C – I Found U (Fono Remix)

@graph.description: Axwell's piano-lit house anthem distilled to under three minutes: a rolling bassline, a gospel-tinged vocal from Max'C and a chorus built for arms in the air.
@graph.headline: Axwell, Max C - I Found U (Radio Edit)

citation.name: 22e cérémonie des Victoires de la musique

@graph.description: Ayọ pleads for a lost love over acoustic guitar and a gentle reggae lilt: the 2006 debut single, recorded with a live band in five days in New York, that made a German-Nigerian singer a star in France.
@graph.headline: Ayọ - Down On My Knees

citation.name: ayokay chart history: Hot Dance/Electronic Songs

@graph.description: Bright synths and Quinn XCII's easy vocal paint a memory of summers when you and your friends felt untouchable: the 2016 breakthrough of two school friends from Michigan.
@graph.headline: ayokay, Quinn XCII - Kings of Summer

citation.name: BAKERMAT releases his highly anticipated second album 'The Spirit' on vinyl
Amsterdam producer Bakermat returns with his 2nd studio album The Spirit

@graph.description: 'The River' is a short, warm house track from Bakermat's second album The Spirit (2021), a record the Dutch producer built from gospel, soul and folk material: a two-and-a-half-minute sketch of uplift rather than a club epic.
@graph.headline: Bakermat - The River

@graph.description: Bright, bouncing and slightly unhinged, Galactical sends Basement Jaxx and singer Vula off into space on a house groove built for dancing in zero gravity.
@graph.headline: Basement Jaxx - Galactical

citation.name: Basement Freaks - Soul Intoxication (Lonely Boy's Detox Dub)
Basement Freaks - Funk From The Trunk

@graph.description: Los Angeles producer Lonely Boy strips a funk track by the Greek producer Basement Freaks down to a hypnotic house dub, issued on Jalapeno Records in 2013 and later picked up by French lounge compilations.
@graph.headline: Basement Freaks - Soul Intoxication (Lonely Boy's Detox Dub)

citation.name: Ben Khan's debut disc full of dizzying grooves, curious funk

@graph.description: Two and a half minutes of warped, woozy funk: Ben Khan's cool falsetto slides over wobbling synths, guitar stabs and brass that sounds trapped inside a bubble.
@graph.headline: Ben Khan - Savage

@graph.description: A strutting, paranoid electro-rock stomp where Joywave's Daniel Armbruster sneers the hook over clipped funk guitar, heavy handclaps and a bassline built for headphones and dance floors alike.
@graph.headline: Big Data, Joywave - Dangerous

@graph.description: Before her solo career, Björk sang Icelandic popular songs and jazz standards with a veteran piano trio: Kata rokkar, from the 1990 album Gling-Gló, is a short, playful glimpse of that side of her voice.
@graph.headline: Björk - Kata rokkar

citation.name: The Hanging Tree (The Hunger Games song)

@graph.description: Blankets carries the Mockingjay murder ballad out of the woods and onto the dancefloor: a 2015 French electronic cover that keeps the song's hummable, unsettling melody and sets it to a pulsing beat.
@graph.headline: Blankets - The Hanging Tree

citation.name: RAC wins Grammy for re-work of Bob Moses' Tearing Me Up
Bob Moses release video for Tearing Me Up

@graph.description: Bob Moses stretch a smoky, heartsick vocal across a slow-burning deep house groove, all brooding guitar, rolling bass and late-night tension that never quite breaks; its RAC remix won a Grammy.
@graph.headline: Bob Moses - Tearing Me Up

citation.name: The Magician and Bobby Nourmand talk tastemaking, Magic Tapes, and the release of 'Smokin Joe'
Bobby Nourmand - S M O K I N' J O E

@graph.description: A laid-back, smoky slice of deep house where a rolling bassline meets a bluesy vocal: the Los Angeles producer's mystery track from The Magician's Magic Tapes, released on Potion in 2016.
@graph.headline: Bobby Nourmand - Smokin' Joe

@graph.description: A crunching dance-rock riff, a strutting beat and a hook about the way you move: Bodyrockers' 2005 floor-filler is pure, unashamed swagger.
@graph.headline: Bodyrockers - I Like The Way (Radio Edit)

citation.name: Not Today (Bonaparte, Acid Pauli), release credits

@graph.description: Berlin's dance-punk ringmaster Bonaparte and the electronic producer Acid Pauli, once of The Notwist, trade a sly, defiant refrain in a 2020 single that sings from the point of view of something humanity has wronged and now asks for rescue.
@graph.headline: Bonaparte, Acid Pauli - Not Today

citation.name: Branko Gives Global Club Music Lesson on Debut 'Atlas' LP
Branko - Made of Gold (feat. SKIP&DIE & Fellow)

@graph.description: Branko's global club sound in miniature: an Amsterdam meeting with SKIP&DIE and Fellow on his debut album ATLAS, a gleaming, bass-heavy groove built for a crowd.
@graph.headline: Branko, SKIP&DIE, Fellow - Made of Gold

citation.name: Brazilian Girls' 'Karaköy' Is A Teary Daydream

@graph.description: A walking-pace daydream named after an old Istanbul harbour district: Sabina Sciubba's supple voice and soft trumpets carry a song of wandering and missing someone, from Brazilian Girls' 2018 comeback album Let's Make Love.
@graph.headline: Brazilian Girls - Karaköy

citation.name: Today's Song: Happiest Man On Earth – Broken Back
Broken Back – Happiest Man On Earth (FDVM Remix)

@graph.description: Bright acoustic strumming over a gentle electronic beat, Broken Back's first single sounds like optimism earned the hard way.
@graph.headline: Broken Back - Happiest Man on Earth (Radio Edit)

citation.name: Bronski Beat: The Age of Consent (reissue review)

@graph.description: Bronski Beat's 1984 debut single turns a gay teenager's escape from home into a falsetto-led synth-pop anthem, built on a sequenced octave pattern and remembered for Bernard Rose's stark video.
@graph.headline: Bronski Beat - Small Town Boy

@graph.description: 'Because of You' by C2C featuring Pigeon John is a bright collision of hip-hop, electronics and soul from four French world-champion turntablists, with the Los Angeles rapper's warm voice riding a beat built by hand on record decks.
@graph.headline: C2C feat. Pigeon John - Because of You

@graph.description: Soft beats, sunny loops and a sampled Son House blues voice: Ourson is a short, cuddly piece of French chillout, first a 2015 single and later part of Sputnik II, that feels like a teddy bear rendered in warm sound.
@graph.headline: Camel Power Club - Ourson

citation.name: C.A.R. - Remixes Pt. 1 (Les Disques De La Mort)

@graph.description: Roman Flügel turns C.A.R.'s cold-wave Idle Eyes into patient, hypnotic minimal house: a rattling bassline, spiralling keys and pads that swell slowly toward a euphoric peak.
@graph.headline: C.A.R - Idle Eyes (Roman Flügel Remix)

@graph.description: Caravan Palace's 2015 single fuses 1930s-style swing with club beats and Zoé Colotis's voice, and its animated video of a brawl in a bar full of animals made it one of the most-watched electro-swing tracks ever.
@graph.headline: Lone Digger | Caravan Palace

citation.name: Cardi B - WAP feat. Megan Thee Stallion [Official Music Video]

@graph.description: 'WAP' is a bold and provocative hip-hop track by Cardi B featuring Megan Thee Stallion: a minimal beat, a looped Baltimore club chant and two rappers trading explicit, joyfully unapologetic verses about desire.
@graph.headline: Cardi B - WAP (feat. Megan Thee Stallion)

@graph.description: 'Star Guitar' is The Chemical Brothers' slowly blooming 2002 single, built on four bars of acoustic guitar sampled from David Bowie's 'Starman', and the song behind Michel Gondry's famous one-shot train-window video.
@graph.headline: The Chemical Brothers - Star Guitar

@graph.description: The Chemical Brothers hand the microphone to Fatlip of The Pharcyde for a deadpan rap about a fish-inspired dance: a bubbling, funky detour on their Grammy-winning 2007 album We Are the Night.
@graph.headline: The Chemical Brothers - The Salmon Dance

@graph.description: Chet Faker's smoky late-night soul over a slow, finger-snapping electronic groove, a minimal track that gets all its heat from his weathered voice and a bassline that barely moves.
@graph.headline: Chet Faker - Gold

citation.name: Album Review: Chet Faker - Built On Glass

@graph.description: A wistful, treated saxophone line, a lazy, warm beat and Chet Faker's husky croon make this Built on Glass lead single the definition of late-night electronic soul, and triple j's number one song of 2014.
@graph.headline: Chet Faker - Talk Is Cheap

citation.name: Chicks On Speed / Mäuse - Euro Trash Girl
Chicks On Speed - Chicks On Speed Will Save Us All!

@graph.description: Munich art collective Chicks On Speed turn Cracker's 1990s alt-rock road song into a deadpan electronic cover: an early electroclash single, first pressed on their own Go Records in 1998.
@graph.headline: Chicks On Speed - Euro Trash Girl

citation.name: Chris Lorenzo fuses drum 'n' bass and garage on 'Take Me As I Am'
The Streets share gritty new track "Take Me As I Am"
None of Us Are Getting Out of This Life Alive

@graph.description: Birmingham bass producer Chris Lorenzo and The Streets' Mike Skinner meet on a fast, ferocious slice of drum and bass: tight drums, tearing bass synths and Skinner's dry, conversational vocal.
@graph.headline: Chris Lorenzo & The Streets - Take Me as I Am

citation.name: LAMP Weekly Mix #130 feat. CLAAP! & Santana
CLAAP! Le duo français sort son nouveau single "Vraiment"

@graph.description: A slow Sunday-afternoon deep house cut from a Paris duo's debut EP on La Belle Records, all warm chords, an unhurried beat and Santana's soft vocal drifting in and out of the haze.
@graph.headline: CLAAP!, S.A.N.T.A.N.A. - Dimanche

byArtist.name: Claptone, Clap Your Hands Say Yeah

citation.name: The Beatport chart report: Claptone's mysterious magic
Claptone - Ghost feat. Clap Your Hands Say Yeah (Official Video)

@graph.description: Claptone sets Alec Ounsworth's fragile, quavering indie vocal over a patient deep house groove, a dancefloor track that sounds like it is mourning something.
@graph.headline: Claptone, Clap Your Hands Say Yeah - Ghost

@graph.description: 'Biggest & The Best' is the lead single from Clawfinger's 1997 self-titled album: Swedish-Norwegian rap metal with industrial programming, aimed squarely at people who think they are almighty.
@graph.headline: Biggest & The Best | Clawfinger

citation.name: Cléa Vincent: A Shining New Star in the French Pop Firmament

@graph.description: Cléa Vincent turns Ace of Base's 1992 hit into breezy, homespun French synth-pop, trading its reggae-pop strut for a dreamy, lo-fi groove closer to hip-hop and R&B.
@graph.headline: Clea Vincent - All that she wants

citation.name: Codec & Flexor - Time Has Changed (12-inch single)

@graph.description: Cold, pulsing analogue-style synths and a detached vocal make Codec & Flexor's electroclash-era club hit sound like a rave remembered through frosted glass.
@graph.headline: Codec & Flexor - Time Has Changed (Original)

@graph.description: Erfurt's Northern Lite rework Codec & Flexor's electroclash-era club hit for the 2004 remix EP: a six-minute version that keeps the song's cool, detached refrain and gives it the band's own blend of electro and pop.
@graph.headline: Time Has Changed (Northern Lite Remix) - Codec & Flexor

@graph.name: Get Ready for the Young Folks

citation.name: Get Ready, We're On Our Way

@graph.description: A 2007 mashup by the San Jose producer Controller 7 that lays the Temptations' 1966 'Get Ready' a cappella over the rhythm section of Peter Bjorn and John's 'Young Folks', two songs forty years apart that line up uncannily well.
@graph.headline: Controller 7 - Get Ready for the Young Folks

@graph.description: Corinne Bailey Rae's sun-dappled soul-pop single is a gentle invitation to let your hair down, all breezy guitar, soft horns and a warm voice telling you to grow into yourself.
@graph.headline: Corinne Bailey Rae - Put Your Records On

@graph.description: One phrase, one bassline and seven minutes of repetition: Around the World is Daft Punk proving that a loop can be a whole world on its own, and Michel Gondry's video turned its arrangement into choreography.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Around the World

citation.name: Daft Punk - The Collaborators - Episode 1 - Giorgio Moroder (Official Video)
Daft Punk unveils the first episode in 'The Collaborators' video series; Giorgio Moroder featured
Watch An Interview With Giorgio Moroder For Daft Punk's New Web Video Series
Daft Punk's 'Random Access Memories' Collaborators: Giorgio Moroder
Giorgio Moroder Discusses Collaborating On Daft Punk's New Album 'Random Access Memories'
Daft Punk releases Episode 1 of Collaborator Series: Giorgio Moroder
Daft Punk share five-part mini-documentary series about the collaborators on 'Random Access Memories'

@graph.description: Giorgio Moroder opens Daft Punk's Collaborators films, remembering the Moog, the dance floor and the perfectionism of the two Frenchmen who brought him back into the studio for Random Access Memories.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Episode 1, Giorgio Moroder

citation.name: Daft Punk - The Collaborators - Episode 3 - Nile Rodgers (Official Video)
Daft Punk Collaborators Part 3: Nile Rodgers, 'Groove is everything'

@graph.description: Nile Rodgers tells his own story in the third of Daft Punk's Collaborators films, a warm, funny portrait of the guitarist whose rhythm runs through Random Access Memories.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Episode 3, Nile Rodgers

@graph.description: Recorded live at Bercy, Daft Punk fold the sunny house bounce of Face to Face into the jittery robot funk of Short Circuit, and the pyramid crowd goes up with it.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Face to Face / Short Circuit

@graph.description: Giorgio Moroder tells his own origin story over a click track, then Daft Punk unfold nine minutes of arpeggiated disco, live drums and strings into a time-travelling tribute to the sound he invented.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Giorgio by Moroder

citation.name: First Listen - Daft Punk, Random Access Memories

@graph.description: The curtain-raiser of Random Access Memories: live drums, Nile Rodgers' guitar and a vocoder mission statement announcing that Daft Punk came back to make music breathe again.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Give Life Back to Music

@graph.description: A chopped funk loop and a robot reciting a workout mantra: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger is Daft Punk turning a sample into one of the most quoted hooks of the century.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk - Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger

@graph.description: Nile Rodgers' chicken-scratch guitar, Pharrell's easy vocal and Daft Punk's robot choir turn a four-chord loop into the most irresistible disco revival of the 2010s: the lead single of Random Access Memories, in its radio edit.
@graph.headline: Daft Punk, Pharrell Williams, Nile Rodgers - Get Lucky (Radio Edit)

citation.name: David Lynch - "Pinky's Dream" (Feat. Karen O) (Trentemøller Remix)
Visionquest gives David Lynch's Pinky's Dream a sleek electro overhaul

@graph.description: Trentemøller strips Karen O away and leaves only the nightmare: a throbbing, sinister synth drive that sounds like a car speeding down a Lynchian highway at night.
@graph.headline: David Lynch, Karen O - Pinky's Dream (Trentemøller Remix Instrumental)

inAlbum.name: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death

@graph.description: Dead Kennedys' 1981 single sets Jello Biafra's satire of a moronic party over East Bay Ray's breakneck surf-punk riff, and became the first UK top-40 hit with the word in its title, despite a BBC ban.
@graph.headline: Dead Kennedys - Too Drunk to Fuck

@graph.description: Depeche Mode's jagged litany of mistakes, hammered out live in Barcelona with snarling synths, live drums and Dave Gahan relishing every bad decision.
@graph.headline: Depeche Mode - Wrong (Live in Barcelona)

inAlbum.name: Late Night Tales: Nightmares on Wax

citation.name: Late Night Tales: Nightmares On Wax

@graph.description: Seven unhurried minutes of Pacific dub-soul from two Fat Freddy's Drop mainstays, Joe Dukie's honeyed voice drifting over a deep, patient bassline built for the small hours.
@graph.headline: DJ Fitchie, Joe Dukie - Midnight Marauders

@graph.description: Fernanda Porto's breezy bossa melody rides a rolling São Paulo drum and bass break, sunlit samba swing meeting rattling breakbeats and deep sub-bass.
@graph.headline: DJ Patife - Sambassim (DJ Patife Remix)

citation.name: DJ S.K.T - Must Be A Reason (Radio Edit)

@graph.description: DJ S.K.T rebuilds the vocal hook of Wamdue Project's 1999 number one King of My Castle into a tight, sunny 2017 house edit for DFX, using a replayed sample rather than the original master.
@graph.headline: DJ S.K.T - Must Be A Reason (Radio Edit)

@graph.description: Drake trades bars with Kanye West, and two lines with Jay-Z, over a murky, minimal trap-inflected beat: a cool, understated flex from the Views era that exists in three different versions.
@graph.headline: Drake, The Throne - Pop Style

citation.name: Dusty Kid - A Raver's Diary (2020 reissue)

@graph.description: The Sardinian techno producer closes his debut album A Raver's Diary (Boxer, 2009) with an unexpected, tender song of layered guitars and his own fragile voice that swells into a wall of sound.
@graph.headline: Dusty Kid - Nemur (Walls of Guitars) (Extended Version)

@graph.description: A plucked marimba-like loop, a dancehall bounce and a flirtation that starts at the bar: Shape of You is the minimal pop machine that took over the world in 2017.
@graph.headline: Ed Sheeran - Shape of You

@graph.description: A piano-driven, falsetto-led romp produced by Danger Mouse, 'This Head I Hold' was Electric Guest's 2012 debut single: retro soul-pop swagger wrapped around a reminder that you don't have to follow the steps society lays out.
@graph.headline: Electric Guest - This Head I Hold

@graph.description: Eli Meltzer, better known as the Bay Area rapper and producer Smoov-E, borrows the swagger of early rock and roll for a short, cocky chase song built on one taunting refrain.
@graph.headline: Eli - Faster You Fall

inAlbum.name: Halfway Between the Gutter and the Stars

citation.name: Fatboy Slim - Sunset (Bird of Prey) [Official 4K Video]

@graph.description: 'Sunset (Bird of Prey)' is Fatboy Slim's 2000 single built around Jim Morrison's voice, sampled from the Doors' 'Bird of Prey': a slow-rising, sun-bleached dance track whose video sends a 1960s fighter pilot on a hallucination.
@graph.headline: Sunset (Bird of Prey) | Fatboy Slim

@graph.description: Faul & Wad Ad build a sax-lit, bittersweet house groove around the children's-choir refrain of Pnau's Baby, a song about growing up that became a European number one.
@graph.headline: Faul & Wad, PNAU - Changes

@graph.description: The first single from Feist's The Reminder (2007), co-written and produced with Chilly Gonzales: a sly, piano-led indie pop song about love and longing, danced through an empty airport at night in Patrick Daughters' video.
@graph.headline: My Moon My Man | Feist

@graph.description: 'Madame Hollywood' by Felix Da Housecat featuring Miss Kittin is an electroclash single that plays the glamour of stardom deadpan: a Chicago house producer's taut electro beat and a French voice that sounds bored by fame.
@graph.headline: Felix Da Housecat - Madame Hollywood (feat. Miss Kittin)

citation.name: Felix Da Housecat - Silver Screen Shower Scene
David Guetta, Felix Da Housecat, and Kittin breathe new life into 2001 house classic

@graph.description: Felix Da Housecat's 2001 electroclash single: a melody sampled from The Flirts' 'Passion', Miss Kittin's cool, spoken-sung vocal and a lyric of starlets and cameras, the record that opened Kittenz and Thee Glitz.
@graph.headline: Felix Da Housecat - Silver Screen (Shower Scene)

@graph.description: Fernanda Porto's own Sambassim: the São Paulo composer's song that fused samba and bossa nova melody with electronic beats and helped name a style, drum 'n' bossa.
@graph.headline: Sambassim | Fernanda Porto

citation.name: Filous puts his own chill spin to Gorillaz's classic 'Feel Good Inc.'
Listen to Filous' cover of the Gorillaz 'Feel Good Inc.'
Five Good Covers: Feel Good Inc. (Gorillaz)

@graph.description: The Austrian producer filous strips the Gorillaz classic down to a delicate xylophone, plucked strings and airy beats, and LissA's light voice turns the old windmill anthem into a hazy daydream.
@graph.headline: filous, LissA - Feel Good Inc.

@graph.description: 'Emerge' is Fischerspooner's debut single and one of the defining records of electroclash: a pounding, theatrical electro-pop anthem from a New York duo that began as a performance art piece about entertainment.
@graph.headline: Fischerspooner - Emerge

@graph.description: The neo-house track that introduced FKJ: chopped vocals, warm filtered chords and an elastic bassline wrapped into four and a half minutes of slow-burning, sunlit intimacy.
@graph.headline: FKJ - Lying Together

citation.name: Freddie Gibbs features on new Flume remix

@graph.description: A chopped-up soul vocal, wobbling synth chords and a swinging, head-nodding beat: Flume's breakout cut is two and a half minutes of pure, woozy elation.
@graph.headline: Flume - Holdin On

@graph.description: A rubbery, swaggering tech-house stomper from Berlin's Format:B, built on a fat bassline and chopped vocals from Shorty Long's 1966 Motown single Function at the Junction, cut down to a radio-sized strut.
@graph.headline: Format:B - Chunky (Radio Edit)

@graph.description: 'Remember The Name' by Fort Minor is an anthem of perseverance: Mike Shinoda and Styles of Beyond trade verses over a cello loop and a chorus that breaks success down into percentages, a song that became the soundtrack of sport.
@graph.headline: Fort Minor - Remember The Name

@graph.description: A breezy, whistled indie-pop earworm with a chilling story underneath: the demo Mark Foster wrote and recorded alone in five hours, which went viral in 2010 and spent eight weeks at number three in the US.
@graph.headline: Foster The People - Pumped Up Kicks

Gabriella Cilmi - Lessons To Be Learned (digital edition)

citation.name: Gin Wigmore releases new video for Written in the Water: Live However

citation.name: Listen: Glass Animals share Gilligan Moss Gooey remix

citation.name: Hania Rani - Full Performance (Live on KEXP)

Simon Carpentier du groupe Her est décédé

Him_Self_Her - Gone Too Long (Original Mix) CROSSTOWN REBELS

@graph.headline: Him_Self_Her, Kieran Fowkes - Gone Too Long (Original Mix)

@graph.description: Hindi Zahra's smoky voice glides over a lilting, desert-blues guitar and soft percussion in Beautiful Tango, a slow dance of a song that sounds like dusk in a small room.
@graph.headline: Hindi Zahra - Beautiful Tango (Remastered Version)

@graph.headline: Pilocka Krach - Discolight (Hrdvsion's NSD Mix)

@graph.description: 'FCKRZ' is a 2021 single by the Viennese singer Luca Malina, R&B-inspired pop about the darker side of relationships, produced by Luca Pivetz with guitar by Lukas Koffler and a self-made video.
@graph.headline: Luca Malina - FCKRZ

citation.name: Clip "Cooler Than Me" : Lucky Luke cartonne avec sa reprise de Mike Posner

@graph.description: The Lithuanian producer Lucky Luke's 2019 electro-house reworking of Mike Posner's 2010 debut hit, released on Columbia/B1: a song about feeling snubbed, turned into a laid-back club anthem that became a radio hit in France a year later.
@graph.headline: Lucky Luke - Cooler Than Me

citation.name: Lulu Rouge: Bless You [Music For Dreams]

@graph.description: Danish duo Lulu Rouge and their old ally Trentemøller in seven and a half minutes of nocturnal minimal house: reverberating dub bass, slow-building layers and a Basic Channel shadow.
@graph.headline: Lulu's Theme (feat. Trentemøller)

@graph.description: From Lulu Rouge's 2008 debut Bless You, a slow, dub-shadowed Copenhagen downtempo track in which Alice Carreri sings Mikael Simpson's words over deep bass and spacious, echoing textures.
@graph.headline: Sweeter Than Sweet (feat. Alice Carreri)

@graph.description: The closing track of Mafia Klvb's 2022 debut, made with Pilocka Krach and Mommo G: underground lifestyle rap that turns the credit card into a symbol of excess and the persona into the point.
@graph.headline: Mafia Klvb - Credit Card

@graph.description: Mando Diao trade garage-rock grit for a disco-rock floor-filler, a pulsing four-to-the-floor beat and a shout-along chorus about needing someone to dance with.
@graph.headline: Mando Diao - Dance With Somebody (Radio Version)

citation.name: Review: Marbert Rocel – Catch a Bird

@graph.description: A soulful downtempo song from the German trio Marbert Rocel's second album Catch A Bird: Antje Seifarth's gentle voice over soft, slowly unfolding electronics, made for winding down.
@graph.headline: Marbert Rocel - Hush Now

@graph.description: An eighteen-minute minimal track by the Romanian producer Marcu Rareș, the title piece of his 2018 EP for the Romanian minimal techno label Welter Records.
@graph.headline: Marcu Rares - Camimosa

citation.name: Chet Faker And Marcus Marr Share Birthday Card

@graph.description: Nearly eight minutes of sleek, disco-tinged house: Marcus Marr's springy production and bright synths carry Nick Murphy's smoky voice towards a long dancefloor release, the opener of their 2015 EP Work.
@graph.headline: Marcus Marr, Nick Murphy - Birthday Card

@graph.description: Marcus Marr and Chet Faker (Nick Murphy) recorded this disco-funk jam in four days in a Brixton studio in July 2015: a funk-flecked guitar riff and a soulful plea about a relationship going wrong, made into a reason to dance.
@graph.headline: Marcus Marr, Nick Murphy - The Trouble With Us

@graph.description: Nine minutes of melodic German minimal from the Jena label Freude am Tanzen: Marek Hemmann's Gemini drives on a swinging house groove while synth patterns and funky tenor-sax licks twist around each other.
@graph.headline: Marek Hemmann - Gemini

citation.name: Premiere: Soulwax re-writes Metronomy's Love Letters

@graph.description: Soulwax strip Metronomy's sixties-tinged pop down to a gleaming machine groove and rebuild it, six and a half minutes of neon disco-pop driven by the bassline and a slow-burning release.
@graph.headline: Metronomy - Love Letters (Soulwax Remix)

inAlbum.name: HIStory - Past, Present and Future, Book I

@graph.description: One of pop's most recognisable bass lines carries Michael Jackson's paranoid tale of a paternity claim, a tight, shadowy groove that sounds as sharp now as it did on Thriller.
@graph.headline: Michael Jackson - Billie Jean

citation.name: I may actually be writing the same song over and over: an interview with Michelle Gurevich

@graph.description: A slow, smoky synth ballad in which Michelle Gurevich's deadpan contralto toasts the giddy first months of a romance while already hearing the ending coming.
@graph.headline: Michelle Gurevich - First Six Months of Love

@graph.description: Michelle Gurevich croons a deadpan, candlelit elegy for love gone cold, with lo-fi synths and a slow-dance sway that make heartbreak feel strangely elegant.
@graph.headline: Michelle Gurevich - Lovers Are Strangers

@graph.description: 'Party Girl' is the home-recorded title song of Michelle Gurevich's 2007 debut, made under the name Chinawoman: a slow, deadpan contralto ballad about nightlife that became her best-known song and gave its title to a Cannes-winning film.
@graph.headline: Party Girl | Michelle Gurevich

citation.name: Mickey Avalon - "Speak of the Devil" review
Rock n roll rapper Mickey Avalon releases Dodging Bullets video featuring Landon McNamara

@graph.description: A darkly comic outlaw ballad from Mickey Avalon's 2020 album Speak of the Devil, produced by Eli Meltzer as Smoov-E: two small-town boys, a shovel and a getaway, over a jangly guitar and a refrain that nothing in this world is free.
@graph.headline: Mickey Avalon, Eli - Ultra-Violence

@graph.description: Miike Snow's 2012 lead single sets sing-along melancholy over glitchy piano chords and a four-on-the-floor house beat, recorded in a Stockholm studio once used by ABBA.
@graph.headline: Miike Snow - Paddling Out

@graph.description: Mirwais, the former Taxi Girl guitarist who would soon produce Madonna's Music, sets a vocoded voice against stop-start acoustic guitar and retro synths: a 2000 French electro single that reached number two on the US club chart.
@graph.headline: Mirwais - Naïve Song

citation.name: First Album (Miss Kittin & The Hacker album)

@graph.description: 'Frank Sinatra' is one of the founding anthems of electroclash: Miss Kittin's deadpan spoken vocal over The Hacker's raw electro, a cool, satirical portrait of fame and excess that still fills dancefloors.
@graph.headline: Miss Kittin - Frank Sinatra

citation.name: An Interview with Headman of Relish Recordings

@graph.description: Headman's own club version of Moisture, his song with the singer Luca Santucci: a sleek, hypnotic nu-disco and house groove stretched for the dance floor, a bonus track on the 2016 deluxe edition of his album ON.
@graph.headline: Headman, Luca Santucci - Moisture (Headman Club Version)

@graph.description: A smouldering piece of dark synth-pop that opens Mount Sims' 2004 album Wild Light: cold machines and a weary croon circle the remains of something that burned out long ago.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Ashes

@graph.description: Deadpan vocals, buzzing analog synths and a drum machine with attitude: Good Service is Mount Sims serving early-2000s electroclash with a sly, suggestive grin.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Good Service

@graph.description: A slow, cold-blooded crawl through synths, live drums and a graveside croon: Grave, from the 2008 album Happily Ever After produced by Thomas Stern, turns Mount Sims' taste for horror into five minutes of nocturnal dread.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Grave

@graph.description: Mount Sims at his most driven: a tight, menacing electro pulse and a vocal set on walking straight into trouble, one of the songs added to Happily Ever After...Again, the 2010 reworking of his darkwave album.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Hellbent

@graph.description: A dark, pulsing piece of electroclash from Mount Sims's 2002 debut UltraSex, released on Gigolo in Europe and Emperor Norton in the US: gritty machine beats, minor-key synth melodies and a cool, defiant vocal.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - How We Do

citation.name: Andy of Jenny (Mount Sims, Jessie Evans), release credits

@graph.description: A short, sharp electroclash track from Mount Sims' 2008 album Happily Ever After, with André Lang's live drums under the synths and the underground punk singer Jessie Evans adding saxophone.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims, Jessie Evans - Andy of Jenny

@graph.description: Mount Sims trades his electroclash gloss for the guitar-driven shadows of his post-punk turn, a short, tense blast of darkwave unease.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - New Authority Volunteers

@graph.description: A night drive with the headlights off: grinding analogue bass, clipped drum machines and Mount Sims' cool, menacing croon from the darker side of electroclash.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - No Yellow Lines

@graph.description: Seven minutes of slow-burning tension, Restless loops a nervous synth figure and a stalking beat until the repetition itself becomes the thrill.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Restless

@graph.description: Cold synth stabs and a deadpan, sneering vocal turn revenge into a dancefloor chant: Mount Sims at his most wiry, sleazy and defiant.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - The Bitten Bite Back

@graph.description: Mount Sims trades the club for a scuffed, shrugging groove, with Toby Dammit of Iggy Pop's and Nick Cave's bands on drums: What's the Big Deal asks its question with a sneer and a beat that will not sit still.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims, Toby Dammit - What's the Big Deal

@graph.description: Cold machine rhythm and a detached croon from the American edition of Mount Sims' 2002 debut UltraSex, an electroclash meditation on being close to someone and still completely on your own.
@graph.headline: Mount Sims - Together Alone

@graph.description: Mélissa Laveaux, a Montreal-born singer-songwriter of Haitian descent, recasts Elliott Smith's bleak 1995 song for percussive finger-style guitar, double bass, claps and drums on her 2008 album Camphor & Copper.
@graph.headline: Mélissa Laveaux - Needle in the Hay

citation.name: Various Artists - The Neptunes Present... Clones

@graph.description: N.E.R.D and Clipse close the Neptunes' Clones compilation with a keyboard-driven rap-rock hybrid: a Queen-sized arena chorus against fast-firing hip-hop verses.
@graph.headline: N.E.R.D, Clipse - Loser

@graph.name: Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)

citation.name: Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)
A Man and His Music – Part II

@graph.description: Nancy Sinatra's 1966 version of Sonny Bono's song, built on Billy Strange's haunting tremolo guitar, is a hushed ballad of childhood love and betrayal that Quentin Tarantino revived over the opening credits of Kill Bill.
@graph.headline: Nancy Sinatra - Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)

citation.name: The White House just joined Spotify: listen to the President's summer playlist

@graph.description: Nappy Roots turn a sunny, soulful beat and a sing-along hook into a Southern porch-step anthem about waking up, counting blessings and hoping today goes right.
@graph.headline: Nappy Roots - Good Day

citation.name: Nicolas Jaar - A Time For Us review

@graph.description: A young Nicolas Jaar's slow, sultry minimal-house classic, a crooned vocal and dusty, swaying textures that famously sink from dance tempo into a long, swooning breakdown nobody wants to mix out of.
@graph.headline: Nicolas Jaar - Time For Us

citation.name: RMX Roundup: Dotan + Niklas Ibach
citation.publisher: Poetry in an Empty Coke Can

@graph.description: Niklas Ibach slips Dotan's aching folk-pop plea onto a soft deep-house pulse, keeping the ache while giving it somewhere to move.
@graph.headline: Niklas Ibach - Hungry (Remix)

citation.name: Nils Ohrmann & Daniel Steinberg - Tumbleweed EP

@graph.description: Six and a half minutes of bumping Berlin house from Nils Ohrmann: a cheeky vocal taunt, a springy bassline and a groove that never lets go.
@graph.headline: Nils Ohrmann - In Ya Face (Original Mix)

@graph.name: Sinnerman (Felix Da Housecat's Heavenly House Mix)

citation.name: Sinnerman (Felix da Housecat's Heavenly House mix)

@graph.description: 'Sinnerman (Felix Da Housecat's Heavenly House Mix)' sets Nina Simone's ten-minute 1965 recording of a traditional spiritual about a sinner with nowhere to hide inside a four-and-a-half-minute house groove, for Verve Remixed 2 in 2003.
@graph.headline: Sinnerman (Felix Da Housecat's Heavenly House Mix) | Nina Simone

@graph.description: Solomun's vocal mix of the Noir & Haze single, Resident Advisor's remix of the year 2011: a rolling, bass-heavy deep house groove under Haze's aching voice, released on Noir Music and later licensed to Defected.
@graph.headline: Noir, Haze, Solomun - Around (Solomun Vox)

@graph.description: The 2001 debut single of Erfurt's Northern Lite, released on their own 1st Decade Records: techno roots turning into electronic pop, with ambient pads, a steady bassline and a slow build toward a driving finish.
@graph.headline: Northern Lite - Trusting Blind

citation.name: Too Drunk to Fuck (Nouvelle Vague recording)

@graph.description: Nouvelle Vague turn the Dead Kennedys' punk satire into a hushed bossa nova sung by Camille, a 2004 cover whose softness makes the lyric more absurd and more unsettling than the original's noise.
@graph.headline: Nouvelle Vague - Too Drunk to Fuck

citation.name: Nu feat. Jo.Ke - Who Loves The Sun (Original Mix) [BAR25-019]

@graph.description: Nine sun-warmed minutes of organic deep house from the Bar 25 world, where Jo.Ke's gentle, sing-along vocal drifts over a loping groove made for golden-hour dancing.
@graph.headline: Nu, Jo.Ke - Who Loves the Sun

inAlbum.name: Do You Want the Truth or Something Beautiful?

@graph.description: Paloma Faith's brassy, swing-tinged retro-soul romp about a world turned on its head, with a stomping rhythm section and a voice that relishes every theatrical flourish.
@graph.headline: Paloma Faith - Upside Down

@graph.description: Paul Oakenfold's breakbeat and hip-house collision with Pharrell Williams: a pulsing, provocative 2006 single about the pull of desire and money, with an animated video that ends in a warning.
@graph.headline: Paul Oakenfold feat. Pharrell Williams - Sex 'N' Money

@graph.description: Peaches at her most gleefully filthy: Pickles rides a stark, rubbery electro beat while she raps about desire with a grin you can hear in every line.
@graph.headline: Peaches - Pickles

@graph.description: Handclaps, a bouncing bassline, Pharrell's falsetto and a gospel-tinged chorus make his Despicable Me 2 song a pure shot of sunshine that became the best-selling song of 2014.
@graph.headline: Pharrell Williams - Happy

@graph.description: The Los Angeles rapper Pigeon John opens his 2010 album Dragon Slayer with The Bomb, a bright, bouncing single co-produced with General Elektriks' Hervé Salters from sampled live instrumentation rather than old records.
@graph.headline: Pigeon John - The Bomb

citation.name: Pilocka Krach - Sugar Cane & The Lost Amigos
Pilocka Krach - Sugar Cane and The Lost Amigos

@graph.description: A track from Pilocka Krach's 2017 double album Sugar Cane & The Lost Amigos, a tour diary pinned between Mexico, Detroit and Berlin: raw sampled cuts and growling synths in the Bar25 veteran's electro post-rave style.
@graph.headline: Pilocka Krach - La Luna Y El Sol

citation.name: Move On (Original Club Mix), release credits

@graph.description: A punchy, no-nonsense club mix from the Swiss house producer Platinum Doug on Enormous Tunes, where a repeated vocal hook and a bouncing bassline push the dance floor forward bar after bar.
@graph.headline: Platinum Doug - Move On (Original Club Mix)

@graph.description: Breathy duet vocals, bright percussive melodies and a lazy tropical groove: Canopée is Polo & Pan's invitation to climb into the treetops and forget the city for four and a half minutes.
@graph.headline: Polo & Pan - Canopée

citation.name: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger | Daft Punk | Pomplamoose

@graph.description: Pomplamoose's 2019 cover of Daft Punk's 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger': a robot anthem built from a sample and a vocoder, replayed by a live band with real keys, bass, drums and human voices, and filmed so that everything you hear, you see.
@graph.headline: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger | Daft Punk | Pomplamoose

citation.name: Portugal. The Man share swinging new single Feel It Still

@graph.description: Portugal. The Man's Grammy-winning sleeper hit: a quick, swinging slice of psychedelic funk-pop that borrows its melody from Motown's Please Mr. Postman and rides one of the decade's most recognisable basslines.
@graph.headline: Feel It Still | Portugal. The Man

@graph.name: Another One Bites The Dust (A Skillz Remix)

citation.name: Another One Bites the Dust (A Skillz remix)

@graph.description: A Skillz chops John Deacon's immortal bassline into a strutting breakbeat workout, keeping Freddie Mercury's swagger front and centre while the drums hit like a b-boy battle.
@graph.headline: Queen, The Miami Project - Another One Bites The Dust (A Skillz Remix)

@graph.description: Recable lifts Angus & Julia Stone's wistful Big Jet Plane onto a gently rolling house groove, keeping the song's daydream of flying away intact.
@graph.headline: Recable - Big Jet Plane (Recable Remix)

citation.name: Robin Schulz feat. Francesco Yates - Sugar

@graph.description: Sun-bleached deep house with a soul hook: Robin Schulz builds a sweet, bouncing groove around Francesco Yates and an interpolation of Baby Bash's 2003 'Suga Suga', a number one in seven countries in 2015.
@graph.headline: Robin Schulz, Francesco Yates - Sugar

@graph.description: A cowbell-clacking, falsetto-laced funk-pop strut from Robin Thicke, Pharrell and T.I. that owned the summer of 2013 and then the courtroom.
@graph.headline: Robin Thicke, T.I., Pharrell Williams - Blurred Lines

@graph.description: The slow, string-laced turn on Róisín Murphy's 2007 electro-disco album Overpowered, co-written with Ill Factor and arranged by Philadelphia soul veteran Larry Gold, heard here in a live performance from the album's era.
@graph.headline: Primitive | Róisín Murphy

@graph.description: The French collective Roseaux and the American soul singer Aloe Blacc turn the Police's 1979 reggae hit into an unhurried soul song, the most famous track of their 2012 album of covers.
@graph.headline: Walking on the Moon | Roseaux

@graph.name: Once Twice feat. Rachel K Collier

citation.name: Ryan Blyth - Once Twice feat. Rachel K Collier
Rachel K Collier, Ableton Certified Trainer

@graph.description: 'Once Twice' is a short, uplifting house track by Ryan Blyth with the Swansea singer and producer Rachel K Collier on vocals, premiered in 2016 on the Love & Other channel: bright beats, a sung topline and a hook built for the dance floor.
@graph.headline: Ryan Blyth - Once Twice feat. Rachel K Collier

citation.name: Santé Shows Us Deeper Shades of House and Techno With Awake

@graph.description: Santé lays a deep, rolling groove under J.U.D.G.E's grave, soulful voice, six minutes of dark-room house that feels like the first clear thought after a long night.
@graph.headline: Santé, Richard Judge - Awake

@graph.description: The title track of Say Yes Dog's 2013 debut EP, later carried onto their album Plastic Love: warm, unhurried synth-pop from a German-Luxembourgish trio who met studying jazz and sound engineering in The Hague.
@graph.headline: Say Yes Dog - A Friend

citation.name: Sleaford Mods - Tweet Tweet Tweet (Live on KEXP)
Sleaford Mods - Divide And Exit; Ten Years On

@graph.description: 'Tweet Tweet Tweet' by Sleaford Mods is a gritty post-punk rant born on a dismal bus ride, aimed at people lost in their phones and at the politics of 2014 England, filmed here live for KEXP in 2023: one man pressing play, one man spitting fire.
@graph.headline: Sleaford Mods - Tweet Tweet Tweet

@graph.description: Solange and Dev Hynes wrap the end of a relationship in a skittering, eighties-tinted R&B groove: the 2012 lead single of the True EP on Terrible Records, with a Melina Matsoukas video shot in Cape Town's Langa township.
@graph.headline: Solange - Losing You

@graph.description: Nine minutes of Solomun's signature deep house, released on his experimental label 2DIY4: Friends rides a supple, swinging groove and moody chords that keep rising just enough to keep a dancefloor leaning in.
@graph.headline: Solomun - Friends

citation.name: Sworn Virgins drop Fifty Dollar Bills
Greased up and ready to go: meet Sworn Virgins

@graph.description: The B-side of the anonymous London disco project Sworn Virgins' 2018 12-inch on Soulwax's DEEWEE label: a driving, chugging late-night cut that The Vinyl Factory called a Harvey-esque freak-out for saturated nightcrawlers.
@graph.headline: Sworn Virgins - Burning Off My Clothes

citation.name: Gnarls Barkley - Crazy (TEEMID & Joie Tan cover)
Teemid - Crazy feat. Joie Tan (Official Music Video)

@graph.description: Gnarls Barkley's frantic classic slowed into a hazy deep-house lullaby: TEEMID and Joie Tan make Crazy sound like a confession whispered at four in the morning.
@graph.headline: TEEMID, Joie Tan - Crazy (Radio Mix)

inAlbum.name: The Sun Ain't Shining No More

@graph.name: The Sun Ain't Shining No More

citation.name: The Sun Ain't Shining No More (recording)

@graph.description: A brassy, technicolour psych-pop stomp from Denmark, Mette Lindberg's helium-bright voice riding horns and a strutting beat that make heartbreak sound like a parade.
@graph.headline: The Asteroids Galaxy Tour - The Sun Ain't Shining No More

@graph.description: The Avener wraps Ane Brun's fragile Scandinavian folk confession in a slow, rolling deep-house groove, turning a private surrender into a sunset dancefloor moment.
@graph.headline: The Avener, Ane Brun - To Let Myself Go

citation.name: The Hacker ft. Mount Sims - Traces / Flesh & Bone (Remixes)

@graph.description: Oxia turns The Hacker and Mount Sims' cold-wave electro into a patient, rolling techno journey, all brooding synth lines and a build that keeps tightening the screw.
@graph.headline: The Hacker, Mount Sims - Traces (Oxia Remix)

@graph.name: One Night In New York City

citation.name: The Horrorist - One Night In N.Y.C.
The Horrorist - One Night In NYC (remixes)

@graph.description: 'One Night In New York City' is The Horrorist's dark techno story of a naive suburban girl's night in the city, first released in 1996 on his own Things To Come label and a German dance number one in 2001, told in a cold spoken voice over a driving machine beat.
@graph.headline: One Night In New York City | The Horrorist

@graph.description: Sting wrote 'Roxanne' after seeing street workers near the band's Paris hotel in 1977: a plea to a woman to leave that life, set to off-beat reggae guitar and a tango-like rhythm, the A&M debut single that became the Police's signature song.
@graph.headline: The Police - Roxanne

byArtist.name: The Supermen Lovers, Herr Styler, Cristine

citation.name: The Supermen Lovers - albums and singles

@graph.description: A flirtatious slice of French pop-funk house from Guillaume Atlan's project, two voices trading lines over a springy bassline until the title becomes a shrugging, grinning verdict on the night.
@graph.headline: The Supermen Lovers, Herr Styler, Cristine - C'est bon

byArtist.name: The Supermen Lovers, Jay Lamar, Jesse Oliver

citation.name: Moments (Jay Lamar & Jesse Oliver Remix), release credits

@graph.description: The Helsinki duo Jay Lamar and Jesse Oliver stretch Moments, a 2013 single by the French producer behind Starlight, into a warm, unhurried deep house glide of soft chords, rounded bass and wistful melodies.
@graph.headline: The Supermen Lovers, Jay Lamar, Jesse Oliver - Moments (Jay Lamar & Jesse Oliver Remix)

@graph.description: A warm slice of French disco-funk from the man behind Starlight, where synths and a rubber-band bassline turn a fleeting moment into a long, glowing groove.
@graph.headline: The Supermen Lovers - Moments

@graph.description: 'Crystalised', The xx's 2009 debut single, is minimal indie pop at its most intimate: a muted guitar riff, a sparse beat by Jamie xx, and two voices, Romy Madley Croft's and Oliver Sim's, answering each other verse by verse.
@graph.headline: The xx - Crystalised

@graph.description: Plucked strings, a chorus of voices and Rotem Bar Or's raw tenor make this Tel Aviv folk song feel like a lullaby sung in a dark, uneasy time.
@graph.headline: theAngelcy - My Baby Boy

citation.name: Tiggs Da Author: Run follow-up Georgia live for Gigwise session

@graph.description: Tiggs Da Author's raspy, swaggering vocal rides a vintage soul feel and a hip-hop bounce on the 2015 love song, produced by Show N Prove, that followed his first single Run and became his breakthrough.
@graph.headline: Tiggs Da Author - Georgia

@graph.description: Timo Maas's 'Shifter', featuring MC Chickaboo, is a driving 2002 single from his debut album Loud: German club production at the meeting point of house and breakbeat, with an MC riding the groove; a UK top 40 hit.
@graph.headline: Timo Maas - Shifter

@graph.description: 'Sandburg', German for sandcastle, is the title track of the Berlin producer Tinush's 2014 EP on Crosswalk: seven minutes of melodic deep house, later cut to a three-minute radio edit, with remixes by Alec Troniq and Umami.
@graph.headline: Tinush - Sandburg

@graph.description: Orlando Higginbottom's breakthrough as Totally Enormous Extinct Dinosaurs: lush synths, a dance-floor pulse and Luisa Gerstein's voice, first on a 2010 Greco-Roman EP and then a 2011 Polydor single that soundtracked Nokia's Lumia adverts.
@graph.headline: Totally Enormous Extinct Dinosaurs - Garden

@graph.description: The queer electropunk duo Tubbe, who moved from Munich to Berlin in 2013, set the small-town dream of the big city against its confetti, noise and 1-euro-shop reality, a 2015 synth-pop single from their Audiolith album Keine Arbeit lieber Tanzen.
@graph.headline: Tubbe - In Berlin

@graph.description: 'Tum Rakak' is a song by Deluxe, the moustachioed band from Aix-en-Provence: a funky live-band groove in B-flat minor with Liliboy singing a gleefully absurd lyric about curiosity, party crumbs and a truck that reeks in the heat.
@graph.headline: Deluxe - Tum Rakak

citation.name: Four Tet remixes 'Smalltalk' by Nigel Godrich's Ultraísta project

@graph.description: 'Smalltalk' is the 2012 lead single of Ultraísta, the trio of Radiohead producer Nigel Godrich, drummer Joey Waronker and singer Laura Bettinson: layered synthesizers and afrobeat-minded drums under a plea to stop the small talk, heard here in Four Tet's garage-shuffle remix.
@graph.headline: Ultraísta - Smalltalk

@graph.description: A pulsating electro track from Vitalic's 2001 Poney EP on International DeeJay Gigolo: driving machine beats and a snarling synth riff that capture the raw energy of the early-2000s dance floor.
@graph.headline: Vitalic - You Prefer Cocaine

@graph.description: Waldeck sets Zeebee's smoky voice inside a crackling, sepia-toned ballroom swing, a downtempo daydream about a love that only lives on in memory.
@graph.headline: Waldeck - Memories

@graph.description: 'Midsummer Night Blues' is a song from Viennese producer Waldeck's 2007 album Ballroom Stories, written and sung by Zeebee: late-1920s ballroom swing seen through modern production, with the crackle of shellac and a summer night's melancholy.
@graph.headline: Midsummer Night Blues (feat. Zeebee)

citation.name: A New Wave of Musical Fusion with Whilk and Misky

@graph.description: 'Darklands' is one of the first two songs the London duo Whilk & Misky ever wrote: a slow-burning blend of blues guitar, electronic production and a voice that starts quietly and ends up belting, from their 2014 debut EP The First Sip.
@graph.headline: Whilk & Misky - Darklands

citation.name: Whilk and Misky: new wave musical fusion
Whilk & Misky - I Want Your Lovin'

@graph.description: A hushed, smoky vocal floats over plucked folk guitar and a slow electronic pulse, turning a simple declaration of devotion into a late-night confession.
@graph.headline: Whilk & Misky - Babe I'm Yours

citation.name: Premiere: Whilk & Misky - Clap Your Hands
Whilk and Misky - Clap Your Hands

@graph.description: The 2014 breakthrough of the London duo Whilk & Misky: a barefoot, bossa-nova-tinged acoustic song with handclaps for percussion, played on Zane Lowe's Radio 1 show and later carried onto dance floors by a Solomun remix.
@graph.headline: Whilk & Misky - Clap Your Hands

citation.name: A New Wave of Musical Fusion with Whilk and Misky

@graph.description: Whilk & Misky blend acoustic warmth with electronic pulse on this track from My Round, Charlie Dickens' soulful voice and Nima Khaste's production chasing a simple wish: to get what we want.
@graph.headline: Whilk & Misky - Get What We Want

citation.name: Whilk & Misky - I Want Your Lovin'

@graph.description: Whilk & Misky's London soul-pop at its most direct: a warm, swinging groove and a voice that asks for exactly one thing, over and over, until you want it too.
@graph.headline: Whilk & Misky - I Want Your Lovin' (Edit)

@graph.description: WHTKD loops a soulful, pleading vocal over a warm, rolling deep house groove, a track that sounds like late afternoon turning into evening.
@graph.headline: WHTKD - Say to Me

@graph.description: Stimming wraps Yoko Duo's fragile song in velvet: a slow, organic deep house remix full of soft textures, a hushed vocal and the feeling of a room going quiet.

@graph.description: 'Oddity' is a discofied highlight of Zurich producer Zwicker's 2009 album Songs of Lucid Dreamers on Compost Records: propulsive beats, a funky bass line and xylophone under the voice of guest singer Olivera Stanimirov.
@graph.headline: Zwicker - Oddity (feat. Olivera Stanimirov)
